subject: English
title: Reading Rainbow: Level 2
tagline: Read short paragraphs and answer 'who, what, where, why' questions!

stages.name: Stage 1
stages.question: In a story about a boy who lost his dog, who is the main character?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! The boy is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is The boy.

stages.name: Stage 2
stages.question: If a story says 'Thabo ran to the shop before it closed', where did Thabo go?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! To the shop is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is To the shop.

stages.name: Stage 3
stages.question: If a story says 'Lindiwe was happy because she won the race', why was Lindiwe happy?
options: He reached the top of the hill
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! Because she won the race is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is Because she won the race.

stages.name: Stage 4
stages.question: What do we call the place and time where a story happens?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! The setting is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is The setting.

stages.name: Stage 5
stages.question: If a sentence says 'First she packed her bag, then she left for school', what happened first?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! She packed her bag is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is She packed her bag.

stages.name: Stage 6
stages.question: What is the problem in a story usually called?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! The conflict is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is The conflict.

stages.name: Stage 7
stages.question: What do we call the people in a story?
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is Characters.

stages.name: Stage 8
stages.question: What word tells you a story is happening 'yesterday'?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! A past-tense clue word like 'yesterday' is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is A past-tense clue word like 'yesterday'.

stages.name: Stage 9
stages.question: If a character says 'I am scared of the dark', how does the character feel?
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is Scared.

stages.name: Stage 10
stages.question: If a story says 'The rain stopped and the sun came out', what happened after the rain?
options: To tell readers what the story is about
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! The sun came out is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is The sun came out.

stages.name: Stage 11
stages.question: Why do authors write titles for stories?
options: To tell readers what the story is about
stages.correctOption: To tell readers what the story is about
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! To tell readers what the story is about is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is To tell readers what the story is about.

stages.name: Stage 12
stages.question: If a sentence says 'Because it was cold, she wore a jacket', why did she wear a jacket?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! Because it was cold is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is Because it was cold.

stages.name: Stage 13
stages.question: What is the lesson a story teaches sometimes called?
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! The moral is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is The moral.

stages.name: Stage 14
stages.question: If a story says 'Sipho finally reached the top of the hill', what did Sipho do?
options: He reached the top of the hill
stages.correctOption: He reached the top of the hill
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! He reached the top of the hill is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is He reached the top of the hill.

stages.name: Stage 15
stages.question: What punctuation mark do you read with a question in your voice?
options: He reached the top of the hill
stages.correctFeedback: Yes! A question mark is right — onward!
stages.wrongFeedback: Not quite — the answer is A question mark.
